# Appendix A: Keywords and Operator Precedence {#app-keywords}

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_keywords.py. Do not edit. -->

A name in tiko is one of five things, and they follow different rules. A **reserved word** is never a name. A **runtime name** may not be reused at module level. A **contextual word** is a keyword only where its statement expects it. A **fixed-width type name**, like the constant `nullptr`, is predeclared and may be replaced. Everything else is free. The rules below were measured by compiling each word in each position with tiko and with fbc-modern 1.20, and the two give the same answer for every word in every position.

## Reserved words (247) {#app-kw-reserved}

A reserved word cannot name a variable, a constant or a procedure, at module level, inside a procedure or inside a namespace. Case does not matter. The diagnostic is usually `TKO0600: '…' is already declared in this scope`, because the word is declared by the language itself; where the word starts a statement of its own, the parser reports that statement's error instead.

The list includes every **statement and function word** of the classic language — `print`, `open`, `len`, `read`, `name`, `width`, `lock` — and every built-in type name, `double` and `string` included. `function Double( )` is refused, and so is a variable called `read`.

### Keywords as field names {#app-kw-fields}

A **field** may be named by most reserved words, because a field's name is only ever read after `.` or `->`, or in its type's body. A type can have a field called `name`, `type`, `len` or `constructor`, and `t.name` reads it. The exceptions:

- The operator words `and`, `andalso`, `eqv`, `imp`, `mod`, `not`, `or`, `orelse`, `shl`, `shr` and `xor`, and `delete` and `new`, are never field names.
- In the type-first spelling, `as T name`, `const`, `ptr` and `pointer` are part of the type, not a name; `ptr as long` is a field.
- In the name-first spelling, `name as T`, the declaration words `const`, `declare`, `dim`, `enum`, `redim`, `static`, `private`, `protected` and `public` start a declaration instead, and `type` and `union` cannot take array bounds (`type( 0 to 2 ) as long`).
- In the type-first spelling, `alias` is not a name either. `alias as long` is fine.
- `rem` starts a comment where a statement can end, so `rem as long` is a comment. `as long rem` declares a field named `rem`, and `t.rem` reads it.

## Runtime names (104) {#app-kw-runtime}

These are the runtime library's procedures. They are not reserved words. The runtime declares them in the global namespace, so a declaration of the same name at module level collides with it: `TKO0813: '…' is already declared by the runtime library`. That covers a variable, a constant, a procedure, a `for` counter, a local inside a module-level procedure, and a parameter of a procedure's definition. The same name is fine inside a namespace or a method, as a field, a member procedure or an enum member, and as a parameter of a prototype.

|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allocate` | `csrlin` | `fre` | `multikey` | `rnd` | `settime` |
| `beep` | `curdir` | `freefile` | `mutexcreate` | `run` | `shell` |
| `bload` | `date` | `getjoystick` | `mutexdestroy` | `screencopy` | `space` |
| `callocate` | `deallocate` | `getkey` | `mutexlock` | `screenevent` | `stop` |
| `chain` | `dylibfree` | `imageconvertrow` | `mutexunlock` | `screenlist` | `system` |
| `chdir` | `dylibload` | `imagedestroy` | `out` | `screenlock` | `threadcreate` |
| `clear` | `environ` | `inkey` | `pcopy` | `screenptr` | `threadwait` |
| `cls` | `eof` | `inp` | `pmap` | `screenres` | `time` |
| `command` | `erfn` | `kill` | `pointcoord` | `screenset` | `timer` |
| `condbroadcast` | `erl` | `loc` | `pos` | `screensync` | `wait` |
| `condcreate` | `ermn` | `locate` | `randomize` | `screenunlock` | `windowtitle` |
| `conddestroy` | `exec` | `lof` | `reallocate` | `setdate` | `wspace` |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bin` | `getmouse` | `oct` | `screeninfo` | `vallng` | `whex` |

`#define` is the exception: tiko accepts `#define run 5`, where fbc refuses it as a duplicated definition (Appendix D).

## Contextual words {#app-kw-contextual}

FBC-Modern's extensions added these words without reserving them, so existing code that uses them as names keeps compiling. Each one is a keyword only in the position shown, and an ordinary name everywhere else: each one compiles as a variable, a procedure, a field, a local and a namespace member.

| Word | A keyword in |
|---|---|
| `channel` | `select channel` (Chapter 23) |
| `defer` | `defer` statement, when a name, a keyword other than `as`, or the end of the statement follows (Chapter 6) |
| `each` | `for each` (Chapter 20) |
| `from` | `case receive v from ch` in `select channel` |
| `in` | `for each x in …` |
| `of` | type arguments: `Array( of int32 )` (Chapter 17) |
| `override` | after a method's declaration: `declare sub M( ) override` (Chapter 14) |
| `partial` | `partial type` and `partial class`, one type in several blocks (Chapter 15) |
| `receive` | `case receive` in `select channel` |
| `send` | `case send v to ch` in `select channel` |
| `spawn` | `spawn Proc( args )` (Chapter 23) |
| `timeout` | `case timeout ms` in `select channel` |

## Fixed-width type names {#app-kw-fixed}

tiko predeclares ten type names that fbc does not have. They are typedefs, not reserved words (Chapter 4): a program's own declaration of one of them replaces tiko's without a diagnostic, so code that already declares `INT32` — as `win/basetsd.bi` does — compiles unchanged.

| Name | Same type as | Name | Same type as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `int8` | `byte` | `uint8` | `ubyte` |
| `int16` | `short` | `uint16` | `ushort` |
| `int32` | `long` | `uint32` | `ulong` |
| `int64` | `longint` | `uint64` | `ulongint` |
| `float32` | `single` | `float64` | `double` |

## The predeclared constant {#app-kw-nullptr}

tiko predeclares one constant that fbc does not have, `const nullptr as any ptr = 0`: the null pointer, as a pointer (Chapter 11). It is replaced on the same terms as the type names above, so a program's own `nullptr` — fbc's own test suite has a field by that name — compiles unchanged.

## Operator precedence {#app-precedence}

Tightest first. Operators on one row bind equally, and **every binary operator is left-associative**, `^` included. The member operators `.` and `->`, calls `( )` and indexing `[ ]` bind tighter than everything here.

| Level | Operators |
|---:|---|
| 1 | `^` |
| 2 | `-` (sign) `+` (sign) |
| 3 | `*` `/` |
| 4 | `\` |
| 5 | `mod` |
| 6 | `shl` `shr` |
| 7 | `+` `-` |
| 8 | `is` `&` |
| 9 | `=` `<>` `<` `<=` `>` `>=` |
| 10 | `not` |
| 11 | `and` |
| 12 | `or` |
| 13 | `imp` `eqv` `xor` |
| 14 | `orelse` `andalso` |

The table is FreeBASIC's, measured operator pair by operator pair against fbc, and several rows differ from C and from intuition (Chapter 5). Each line below prints the same with tiko and with fbc-modern:

```text
2 ^ 3 ^ 2            64     ^ is left-associative: (2 ^ 3) ^ 2
-2 ^ 2               -4     ^ binds tighter than the sign
1 shl 2 + 1           5     shl binds tighter than +, unlike C's <<
8 \ 4 * 2             1     * binds tighter than \: 8 \ (4 * 2)
2 * 3 mod 4           2     mod is looser than * and \
12 or 10 xor 6        8     or binds tighter than xor
1 or 2 and 0          1     and binds tighter than or
0 andalso 1 orelse 1 -1     andalso and orelse share one level
not 1 = 0            -1     not is looser than the comparisons: not (1 = 0)
not 0 and 3           3     ...and tighter than and: (not 0) and 3
```

`&` binds looser than `+` and `-`, so `"a" & 1 + 2` means `"a" & (1 + 2)`, and both compilers print `a3`.
